entries.title: A mountain for a mouse
entries.literal_meaning: Dig a mountain; kill a mouse.
entries.explanation: The work is mountain-sized, but the result is only a mouse. That sudden reduction supplies the joke. Praharaj’s dictionary applies the saying to much effort yielding little or a negligible result. The expanded reading here also notices the fuss or grand promises surrounding such an outcome. It is the mismatch of scale that matters, rather than a rule that small results are always worthless.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାହାଡ଼ ଖୋଳିବା ଭଳି ବଡ଼ କାମର ଶେଷରେ ମିଳିଲା ମୂଷାଟିଏ। ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିରୁ ଏତେ ଛୋଟ ଫଳ—ଏହି ଅମେଳଟି ହସାଏ। ଅନେକ ହଇଚଇ, ପରିଶ୍ରମ ବା ବଡ଼ କଥା ପରେ ଫଳ ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ଏହି ଛବି ମନକୁ ଆସିପାରେ। ଛୋଟ ଫଳର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ; ଯେତେ ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ହେଲା, ତାହା ସହ ଫଳ ମେଳ ଖାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Grand effort ends in a disproportionately small result.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ଆୟୋଜନର ଫଳ ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ହେବାର ଛବି।
entries.usage_example: After several elaborate meetings, a group changes only the colour of a notice; someone quietly compares the result to a mouse. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly labels this a proverb and supplies the effort-versus-result gloss. The joke about scale and the imagined meeting are editorial expansions. No originating incident or borrowing history is established.

entries.title: When unclear words become scripture
entries.literal_meaning: When Brahma speaks incoherently, it is the Veda.
entries.explanation: The saying makes the speaker’s standing outweigh the clarity of the words. Even incoherent speech is received as scripture when it comes from Brahma. The dictionary places this example under the sense “to speak incoherently” and labels it a Dhaga. The further reading offered here is satirical: a statement can acquire authority merely because of who says it. That is an editorial interpretation of the contrast, not a doctrinal account of the Vedas.
entries.meaning_odia: ବ୍ରହ୍ମା ବିଳିବିଳେଇଲେ ବି ତାହା ବେଦ। କଥା କେତେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ, ତାହାଠାରୁ କିଏ କହୁଛି ସେ କଥା ବଡ଼ ହୋଇଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଅନର୍ଥକ ବାକ୍ୟ କହିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ଏହି ଢଗଟି ଉଦାହରଣ ହୋଇଛି। ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପାଠ ହେଉଛି ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାର ଜୋର ଉପରେ ଏକ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ—ବଡ଼ ଲୋକ କହିଛନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଅସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଭ୍ରାନ୍ତ ଧରିନେବା।
entries.english_summary: A speaker’s prestige can make unclear words seem authoritative.
entries.odia_summary: କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାରେ ଅସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କଥା ବି ପ୍ରମାଣ ହୋଇଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A vague remark by a famous speaker is repeated as a firm rule, although nobody can explain what was meant. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: Brahma and the Veda remain the source’s cultural anchors. The dictionary supports the lexical sense and identifies the example as Dhaga; the prestige-over-clarity interpretation is Project Odisha’s reading. No originating scripture passage or religious teaching is asserted, and the saying is not attributed to Brahma as its author.
